utterances.text: -- whether in fact these statements have those photographs redacted, because at the beginning we agreed we will only have those which are redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statements are not physically redacted because we -- we were going to ask Your Honours if they just -- if they wanted to accept the statement and then disregard in evidence those paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You asked that question at the beginning, ma'am, and I answered you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, you did. But we don't have time to redact them at the moment, so we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So I can put on the record that we will be submitting a redacted statement, and I'll state the paragraphs on the record that are going to be redacted, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you do that, then I would suggest that these statements, 6194 and 6196, be not tendered into evidence, but that the redacted form be the one that is tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can use them to cross-examine --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- as long as you don't cross-examine on those redacted paragraphs, but then Court I think must get documents that are agreed between the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am being advised also that P06194 has attached to it some annexes, like newspaper cuttings, and it is not known whether they form part of the statement or not. Now, can the parties agree on that and make sure that what then does get tendered into evidence is what the parties agree on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would -- we would seek to admit the entire statement, including the attachments to the statement, for the reason that the witness discusses these documents within the statement. So the statement isn't going to make any sense unless Your Honours can see the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would be content for the statements to be admitted with the attachments forming an integral part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could just make one other suggestion as well, because procedurally I'm not sure how it's going to go if I start cross-examining a witness upon a statement which hasn't been introduced into evidence. One proposal I would have is that we admit the three statements now, pointing out the paragraphs to be redacted, and we simply mark them for identification; and, then, at the first opportunity the Prosecution has, they substitute those documents for the redacted versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but for now we have got two statements, not three.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: For now, that's correct, Your Honour. I'm anticipating another one being discussed soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I would imagine that other one is going to be a replacement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, there is a third statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. You know her case. I don't. Okay. So be it. Then the two statements are admitted into evidence. May then they please be given an exhibit number, each one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But would you like me to put on the record the paragraphs that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to 6 -- P06194, the following paragraphs will be redacted: 18, 19, 27, and 32. With respect to P06196, paragraph number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I concur with that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'll move on to the other statement. May the witness please be shown P06195.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you move on, can we have them admitted into evidence and they then be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the statement 65 ter number P06194 will be MFI 642 [Realtime transcript error read in error "6142"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: MFI?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI, marked for identification, as requested by Defence counsel. And 65 ter number P06196 will be MFI 643 [Realtime transcript read in error "6143"].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when the -- when the Prosecution submits, Your Honour, the redacted versions, will they be made automatically into exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we deal with that at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let the record show that these are not exhibits 6142 and 6143 respectively. They are 642 and 643. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, may the witness be shown P06195.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we move up so he may see signatures and date, if it's on here. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: In the English, the date is the 6th of June, 2007. It was signed on the 7th of June, and that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And is this the second statement that you gave to OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is my second statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, again, at the time you provided this statement, did you answer the questions of the investigator truthfully and freely?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I answered truthfully and freely to all of the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then, at the conclusion of this interview, the June of 2007 interview, was the statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreter read it back to me in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you sign at that time the English version of the statement after it had been read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign it. The date is the 7th of June, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you also sign the Bosnian translation in early October of this year, of this statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I signed the statement with the corrections made or included in the corrigendum, in the annex that we have just discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, we ask that this statement and the attachments be admitted into evidence -- or marked for identification when we'll discuss the -- the omitted paragraph numbers. There is one slight issue here, and that is the -- I have a hard copy of the statement that was signed by the witness in Bosnian. I'm not sure why it's not in -- in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were rising on your feet, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. My learned friend makes reference in relation to this statement to "attachments" to the statement, and this is the October [sic] 2007 one, the third one, we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, wait a minute. We're talking about the June 2007 one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. June, 6th of June, 2007. Could my learned friend please clarify what she means by "attachments," because as far as I'm aware, there are no additional attachments attached to this document, unlike the one going back to 2005, which had the series of annexes, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise if I've caused confusion, because my colleague here is showing in fact there were attachments to both the 2005 and the 6th June 2007 document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to state that -- that that's the case. The range of the -- the June 2007 statement includes the area in range that was on the exhibit list includes the attachments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So you want that to be given an MFI exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an MFI exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, MFI Exhibit 644.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's marked for identification; and for the record, the following photographs will be redacted from this statement: 7, 8, 21, 25, and 34. And, in evidence, Your Honour, we would like the signed copy of the Bosnian statement, and I have a hard copy here. So if we could scan it into e-court, that would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute, Madam Vidovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to you, Madam Vidovic. Madam Sartorio, we have just put in three statements into evidence. Now you want to give us a fourth statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It is just a -- it is a translation. It is the 2007 statement that the witness signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There are two 2007 statements. Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, he signed the English version when it was read back to him; then he signed the -- the Bosnian version in October of 2007. utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you go through the motions of getting that statement admitted into evidence before we can then have it. Let's have it as a fourth statement, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's not --

utterances.text: -- I don't understand what you are talking about.

utterances.text: But all I'm saying, all I'm saying is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- what you want to substitute now is something -- is not something that we have been talking about. We have talked about three statements here which are on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now you want to introduce a fourth statement, and I don't know whether your learned friend on the opposite side has a copy of what you now want to put in, and what other changes there are in that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that's why I'm saying is, if you have to, put that statement in as a fourth statement. You have put three already. One more is not going to kill us. I don't know what it is you -- you want to substitute.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I just wanted, for the sake of the record, to have the signed version of this document that you see on your screen right now - it's the exact same document, except it's signed by the witness - and that's all. It's a substitute in e-court. We'll drop it, Your Honour, because of time, and we'll admit the English statement that is signed by the witness and the Bosnian translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, may the witness please now be shown P02964 [Realtime transcript read in error "P09624"]; and, in particular, I would like the witness to be shown page 14, and it's page 27 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify what this document is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is an order of the competent prosecutor from Zenica for the exhumation of bodies in the mass grave of Kamenica in Zavidovici municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this order not part of the evidence that is being tendered pursuant to Rule 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, but we're -- we're seeking to admit a few exhibits in addition to the witness's statement, which we understand that is part of the 92 ter process, that you may introduce the witness's statement; if you want -- wish to ask clarifying questions about the statement, you do that, but I have no clarifying questions; and then, in addition, we're seeking to admit additional documents through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: These documents are not part of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- or are not attached to his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will use this little pause to remind the -- everybody that I've got some problems to follow. One should speak more slowly and respect a pause between a question and an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May -- and, sir, you have -- you've just identified what this document is. Have you seen this document and -- during the course of your -- in your position as a -- as a clerk at the office for missing persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the document during the post-mortem of the bodies that was carried out in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, we ask that this document be admitted into evidence. This particular -- there's actually two documents under P02964. So may the witness be shown page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We're in the same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, it's just that I know that the record wrote it down as "9624." Now I just want to be sure that it's "2964."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the record show that earlier it said 9624.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, it -- it -- if that's what it says, it should be 2964, and may the witness be shown page 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Okay. Are you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm going to admit them both after I ask him about the next two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a rather long exhibit. We don't need the whole exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what page in the English?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: 29, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 15 September 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would we --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask -- before I ask you to go to the third page, I'm going to ask you to identify from the front page what this document is.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This document is a record of handover of mortal remains signed by the office for the missing persons that I signed myself and the federal commission, signed by Zaim Kablar and representatives of the cemetery. That is the third signature. My apologies. That's the third signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we see the signature page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is this -- is your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just for the Judges, because they -- they don't know -- they've never seen this document before, what exactly is this document purporting to do?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The document contains the record of the handover of eight mortal remains exhumated in Kamenica near Zavidovici that had been identified by the DNA method, and this document speaks of the bodies that were on the list of the missing persons of the office of Republika Srpska. That means that we have eight skeletal remains and seven skulls that do not belong to the bodily remains, the skeletal remains.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I don't want to get into the substance of the exhumation at this point. I just want you, to make it clear, you say "turnover." From whom to whom? Where are this -- where are these items going? From what entity to what entity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: From the Federation to Republika Srpska. I represented the commission of Republika Srpska, and the second signatory, Zaim Kablar, represented the federal commission in this case; in other words, the commission of Republika Srpska is taking bodies over from the federal commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, still staying with this exhibit, I would like the witness to be shown page 17, and it's only in English at this point, 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I've -- there's miscommunication in terms of the page numbers that I was given, and I just need to clarify it, if I may. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what context did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is the DNA findings for the person called Radomir Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, again, where did you see this document? Did you receive in the course of your job duties; and if so, who did you receive it from and what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I received this document from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, sir. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before my learned friend goes any further in questioning -- questioning the witness, I note from the outset of this witness's testimony that he doesn't speak English, and I just wonder whether it could be established how the witness knows what the contents of these documents are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, as -- as you heard Defence -- Mr. -- My learned colleague state --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He wouldn't have heard because, as he just said, he doesn't understand English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I assume it was translated to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. The question, sir, is, because your primary language is Bosnian, and I presume you don't speak much English, after -- because I've met with you a few times: How is it that you know what this document is if it is only in English?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: If you'll allow me. I come across such documents every day. I've encountered over 1.000 such reports. This is a DNA report that commissions receive from the DNA laboratory, and we know for a fact which person is in question. We have the number of the DNA findings. We have the KT mark. We have the donors that have donated blood. We know where the bone sample originates from. We know for a fact what this is about. The identification is usually done by forensic experts, pathologists, together with me and the competent judge. So I know exactly what this document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that okay with you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, in fact, in terms of the forensic pathologist, do you see the doctor's name on this document anywhere?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: On this particular document, there is no signature. This is findings that we receive from the DNA laboratory, and the signatures are put on the identification records. This is only a DNA report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, sir, where on the right-hand bottom corner, "final release review," signature, date 11.09.06, there is something that looks like a signature there. Do you know that signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you nod your head, it is not recorded on the transcript. Could you please say verbally whether you are agreeing or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that this is a signature; however, this signature was put in the laboratory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know that signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not familiar with the signature at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And one more question. I wasn't -- disregarding the signature, do you see in the bottom right-hand side the name of any doctor or pathologist with whom you worked with regard to this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. The authorised pathologist here is a lady doctor, Brkic-Silajdzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And one more question about this document: Do you see -- do you -- can you identify from this document the name of the person who provided -- the relative who provided the DNA sample?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. This was the mother. If you can blow it up, I could see the name. I believe that her name was Mila Blagojevic -- I apologise. It is Miljana. I can see it now. The father was Vlado Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness now be shown page-- the next page, page 18. They're all part of one exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're just running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long are you going to be with this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, half an hour, if we can move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: With this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. Well, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. It's time to break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I want to know how long you're going to be with this document. Can we accommodate before you take the break or shall we take the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Probably not. Five, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take the break now. We'll come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. May the witness be shown PT2964, page 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you identify what this document is.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is a DNA report for the bone sample KTA-804200 [as interpreted] Kamenica, and it concerns Radomir Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, is this the same person from -- that was the subject of the DNA report of -- that was on page 17 that you saw just before the break?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, the same person, and the same donors of blood samples.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us why there would be two different -- two separate reports for one person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: In principle, sometimes we even have more than two DNA reports; For example, when we have reassociation, when body is not complete. In that case, the forensic pathologist takes samples from all bone samples that cannot be associated to a certain body, and such samples are marked and sent to the laboratory; and, then, when we receive DNA reports from the laboratory, it will happen that for the same person we will find three or four matching DNA reports, which means that bone samples were taken from several samples for the -- from the same body and sent for analysis. That's why we will have more than one or two DNA reports for the bodies that are not complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. Sir, could you repeat the reference number of this DNA report, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. KTA-248/06, Kamenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, because it had said "KTA-804200."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us what that KTA number stands for?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The KTA number stands for the prosecutor's order to take certain action; and, in this case, the action was exhumation, and this prosecutor's order bore the -- this number, KTA-248/06.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And can you also tell us what the "BR.1-3" stands for, if you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is that, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just below the number KTA-248/06, Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The page I have doesn't have anything written just below it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's a little block below that says "9120425."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. That was in page -- that was in document number 17. I'll ask that question later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Next to the person's name, sir, is "ICMP" ID number. Can you tell us what that is, if you know.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The ICMP number is the indication or the identification of the bone that arrived in the laboratory. The laboratory accords a number to the bone; and, sometimes, as I've already explained to you, three bones reach the laboratory for the same body. Still, all these bones bear different numbers. So this is the number of the bone or the indication for the bone that has arrived in the laboratory. In this case, the laboratory marks or assigns its own number to the bone sample.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, let's go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 17 for a moment. Okay. Just -- it was good enlarged. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If you look at the ID number here, sir, 14464, it does appear, does it not, to be the same number as page 18?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So is your answer -- I'm just trying to get clarification if it's a separate number per bone or a separate number per person or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd be grateful if my learned friend would not lead on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, okay, Your Honour. I'll just --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In accordance with your previous answer, you see that these -- these numbers -- ICMP ID numbers are the same. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is a DNA report for Vlado Blagojevic, son of Rade [as interpreted]. For that body, for that person, there could have been five or even six different bone samples; however, once the matching process is completed and the bone and sample -- and blood samples are compared, then we end up with the ID number of the laboratory, which is 1446 [as interpreted] for this particular person. I don't know whether I have made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have not, sir, because at page 67, starting from line 1, you said: "The ICMP ID number is an identification number for a bone," if I made read it to you. Answer: "The ICMP ID number is an indication or the identification of the bone that arrived in the laboratory. The laboratory accords a number to the bone; and, sometimes, as I've already explained to you, three bones reach the laboratory for the same body. Still, all these bones bear different numbers. So this is the number of the bone or the indication for the bone that has arrived in the laboratory." That differs substantially from what you are now telling us that, this ID number is for the person. So you are not clear. What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we didn't understand each other. Now I have on my monitor a number "1/3," and this is what I was talking about, "1/3."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, what you were being asked about, if we can look. The question to which what I've just read to your answer was: "Next to the persons name, sir, is ICMP ID number. Can you tell us what that is, if you know?" So I don't know where you're talking now of the "1/3." The 1/3 came later, and it wasn't there on the page. I asked the counsel. Counsel said, "No, it's on the previous page." We'll come to 1/3. Can you explain what ICMP ID number stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ICMP ID is the identification number for the person Blagojevic Radomir. This is the number that the laboratory assigns when it has a match; then it assigns the number to the name, and that's the ICMP 14464 for Mr. Radomir Blagojevic. I believe the misunderstanding arises from another thing. On this page, there was no identification of the sample that goes to the laboratory. And as I've already told you, for one person there could be several numbers if we did not know from the beginning that all the bones belonged to the same person. I believe that's the source of our misunderstanding here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then let me ask you this question: Does the laboratory assign a number for each bone of a person, of one person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to the laboratory, I can't tell you what the laboratory does, because I don't have access to the laboratory. I can only tell you about the things that I am involved in and that I'm familiar with, and I can only tell you how many bones we send to the laboratory. What the laboratory does from that point on, I wouldn't be able to comment upon because I don't know. All we receive from the laboratory is a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Given just that answer that you have just given us, are you able to tell us what this number, ICMP ID number, refers to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the ID number of the laboratory that is related to a certain name after the matching process of blood samples and bone samples is completed. That's what I was talking about. There can be several bone samples that are matched in the laboratory to complete one body; and, in this person, it's the body of Radomir Blagojevic, who is finally assigned a -- a number after the identification was completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll ask you to please listen to questions and try to answer as briefly as possible to the question. The answer to my question should have been: Yes, I know, or I don't know. You may proceed, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you just tell us, if you know, what the -- on this document, underneath the "KTA-248/06 Kamenica," what that "BR.1/3" stands for, if you know.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Number "1" is the location. There was one grave, and "3" is the number of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: "3" is the number of bodies, or "3" is the number -- there were three bodies, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The number of the bones from a body that was sent to the laboratory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May -- before -- I have other pages from this exhibit that I want admitted; but for now, I need to move to another exhibit to show the relationship, Your Honour. So we'd like to witness to be shown P02575.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not having this one admitted just yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. Yes, Your Honour. I think if you bear with me you'll see what I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is a list of the persons missing from the territory of Ozren in October 1995 in the course of that month. This is a part of the list of those persons that I received from the investigator of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you received this, or after you have reviewed it, did you do anything with this document, with the contents, with the names that are contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I analysed the list and I compared this list with our database of missing persons. The list suffered certain changes, such as typos contained in certain names or dates of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And did -- and did you make a determination about the persons named in this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I analysed the list and I compared this list with our database of the persons missing from the territory of Ozren, and I concluded on the basis of this list that these were soldiers of the Republika Srpska army who all went missing on the 9th of September, 19 -- on the 10th of September, 1995 from the territory of Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Have you spoken with any of these persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Are you referring to the persons from the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm asking if you have ever found and spoken with any of these persons on this list.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: No. No. They were missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Have you spoken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When do you expect him to have spoken, before they went missing or?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm asking if he found any of the persons on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it's a leading question, Your Honour, so I was going to ask him if he has a conclusion with regard to the persons, but I think he's answered that -- the question. I was trying not to ask a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't think it's leading to say: Were they ever found?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you -- did you have an occasion in the course of your duties to -- to speak with and interact with any family members of these persons on this list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I interviewed members of the families of all of the missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you do other -- other -- what did your investigation consist of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: My role was, upon receiving information from the army, to -- that a certain person had gone missing, or if that person was reported by his or her family as missing, to initiate the process of tracing. First of all, to try and determine what the fate of that person was, whether it is still among the living or is deceased. As for this list here, these were soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska who went missing at Ozren, as I said. Only six of the people from this list were found and identified by using the DNA method.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I beg your pardon. Just a second. That answer is not clear. You're saying only six of the people from this list were found and identified by using the DNA method they were found living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct -- no, no, no. No, no. We only use the DNA method to identify dead people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were found dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But when you say "only six of the people on this list were found," it gives the impression that they were living. You've got to say only six bodies of these people were found, and they were identified by DNA method. So you only found the bodies of six people out of fifty-one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, were these six bodies the subject of a previous document that you were shown and -- and identified as the -- discussing the handover of mortal remains? Are these the six bodies that are the subject of that document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. It is precisely those bodies were -- as discussed, the bodies from this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now I would like to direct your attention to number -- well, first let me ask you this: The -- the documents that we saw, the DNA reports that we just discussed a few moments ago, do you see the name of the person on this list that was the subject of those DNA results?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I believe it is Todorovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, the person that was on the DNA sample we just saw . If you need to is see that again, just say so.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Blagojevic. I don't see that name here. We would have to scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you scroll down, please, so the witness can see the entire list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you see his name, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: No, I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You need to scroll over, please, the document so he can see. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I see number 40, "Radenko Blagojevic".

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is -- what is the number next to this -- the number -- is this -- 19. I can't read the number. Could you tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- just a point of clarification. My learned friend asked the witness to identify the name of a person whose name appeared in the DNA reports, and his name was specified there as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was going to ask that we go back to that report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm getting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- Radomir Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm getting to that. I'll be getting to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please. Can we just see this list, this part of the list where number 40 has been shown?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it's not fully translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, I'm asking for the B/C/S, the handwritten one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was just not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we enlarge it, please: Blagojevic Radenko. And this number you were asking about, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is the number on the right-hand side of the name -- is it -- I see -- it says "19-something." Can you tell us what that number is and what that number represents to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The year of birth and place of birth, Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is this number? What is this year of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person was born in 1965 in Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as you just may have heard, there -- the name on this, number 40, appears -- it says "Blagojevic Radenko." Okay? Is that name -- is that first name different from the name that we just saw on the DNA report; and if so, can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I see no difference. This is Radenko Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we please go back to 2964, page 17. Did I -- 2964. Did I say 14? I meant 17. Can I see 17? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, without -- does this name say "Radomir"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, "Radomir."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Then go back to, please, 2575.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe that says "Radenko." So that's not the same name, is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So can you explain why -- how you concluded that this was the same person if the first name is different.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: My office is in possession of all missing persons from the area of Ozren. There is no Radenko Blagojevic born in 1965 in Vozuca. There was a Radomir. There was no person with the other name as someone who had gone missing on that day. This is what I was explaining a while ago. Together with other clerks from my office, we analysed the list and certain names suffered some changes; for example, there were some typos. As in this case, there was Radenko, or Radomir. In principle, Radenko/Radomir, born in 1965, if checked against our database and the database of ICRC, there is no Radomir. There is another first name there. As for Radenko or Radomir, when we use such names, these two names are basically one and the same name; therefore, this mistake of mine was, of course, inadvertent. It wasn't intentional; however, it is the same name and the same person. There was no other person by the last name of Blagojevic born in 1965 in Vozuca that had gone missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in this connection, I'd like the witness -- this document to be put away for the time being and the witness be shown P02883.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, I just want to find out from the witness: Given your explanations, can you just tell us what the correct name of this person is? Is it Radomir or is it Radenko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the name is Radomir Blagojevic. But, if I may, I had to work with 5.000 different names of missing persons. Please do not expect me to know each and every name by heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question regarding this particular document. You told us that two people on this list, two missing people on this list, you used an identification method that uses DNA tests and thereby were able to identify six bodies. You also told us that you conducted an investigation in order to find the other people that were on this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this inquiry was conducted, were you able to find any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. From this list, I found another person that was not part of the so-called Kamenica group, as we called it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this person alive, or was it somebody who had gone missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... this person's dead body was found. His name was -- well, let me just consult -- or rather, let me try to recall the name. There was another person found from this list whose DNA was identified and the name was assigned to the dead body. Can I see the list, please. Yes, it is Obrad Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I was going to go through each --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But when the Judge finish, I have a question, because I'm confused now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know whether you found any people alive, people who were on this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no one was alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, after the research you carried out, did this cover the entire former Yugoslavia -- territory of the entire former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first, we went looking in the area of Ozren. No one from the list was found alive, ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, basically, you only conducted your research in the Ozren area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, where the persons had gone missing, we searched the wider area. There is no need to look into other locations if we know what our methodology is. Our methodology and practice indicates that it was only there that we could find them. As well as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat the last portion of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge. The translators are asking that the witness repeat the last portion of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The seven persons were found in the wider area of Ozren exactly where they had gone missing. As regards refugee camps, all of the families reported their missing members to the International Red Cross, and all those who remained alive returned a year or two after the war. Twelve years, I believe you will agree, is a very long time for one not to get in touch with his or her family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, sir. You testified that these people were involved in war in Ozren. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. These were all members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, at page 78, lines 23 to 25, you say: "Yes. From this list, I found another person that was not part of the so-called Kamenica group, as we called it." Did you call these people"the Kamenica group"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: When I said that I found another person, I had in mind this list before me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But listen to my question. My question is: Did you call these people who are on this list, did you call them "the Kamenica group"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't call them "the Ozren group."

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: No, we did not. To be more precise, Kamenica or Gostovici. That was the name we assigned to the group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Kamenica and Ozren, are they one and the same place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Kamenica is a micro location within the Ozren area, and Gostovici was in the wider area. Kamenica was a micro location, and these people went missing at that micro location. This is what we referred to. We called them by that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At that micro location, which is Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said, "Kamenica was a micro location, and these people went missing at the micro location. This is what we referred to. We called them by that location." I'm saying the micro location is Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if you know, sir, - I just really want to get clarity, if you do know - do you know when they went missing or when they were involved in the action that resulted to them getting missing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: They went missing on the 10th of September, 1995 in the area of Ozren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You're a little bit ahead of me, because I have going to show a document to the witness to confirm what he said about going missing, because we want to admit that as an exhibit. So -- so I would like the witness to be shown 2 -- 2883, please, and page 79 in English and page 40 in B/C/S -- in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The English isn't up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, can you identify this document for us?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. This is an index card of missing or captured person that we keep at our office.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And from -- what is the source of the information that goes into this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Primarily the source was a report from his unit; then we have the BAZ number, 917893, if I'm not mistaken. That is from the report of the ICRC, meaning that this person was reported missing to the ICRC as well; and then it is also based on the information received by family members concerning his date of birth, place of birth, the place he was last seen at, and the clothes the person was wearing at the moment of disappearance. There is also information on whether the person was found or not. It says "no" here; then we have the category, meaning soldier or civilian. This person was a soldier. These were the -- this was the information, and all other information that we could get our hands on would be introduced into our database and made part of the index card.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down a little bit on the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us here what identifies the mother's name and what that name is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Well, mother, it is Mirjana.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. That's all. And, now, is that the same name that was on the DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, the information on this document -- and you just told us and I don't want to -- you said it came from different sources, but I just want to make it clear for the -- for the record that you didn't -- did you draft this document based on the -- the DNA report or based on this list, or did you draft it from independent sources?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This data was created far ahead of receiving the results of DNA analysis; and, as I said, we collected that from several different sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this particular body and can you -- can you confirm or tell us whether this body was one of the -- the six that you've mentioned; and if so, what -- what does that mean, "one of the six"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. This body is one of the six, meaning that by using the DNA method, it was identified and as such the results were accepted by the family and the body was buried under that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But, no, what I'm trying to get at, sir, is -- again, we've introduced your statement into evidence, and you -- within your statement, you discuss different exhumations that you attended or you participated in. Is this body from one of those exhumations?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This body was exhumed by the federal commission. I took no part in their work.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. But we just talked about the handover. Is this one of the bodies that's in the handover report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know where those bodies came from that were the subject of that handover report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Do you mean where I got it or where they had come from?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Where the bodies had come from.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The bodies were taken over in Visoko. They were exhumed in Kamenica, near Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: All right. And just to follow up on one of the Judge's questions. And I don't -- again, it's in your statement, but you identified in your statement. Do you know how many in total that you have reported missing from your region?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: In the area of Ozren, 460 people went missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you know how many live persons of those -- persons that you found alive of those?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this line of questioning because this is contained within one of the witness statements. So we -- we're really overlapping and duplicating matters by going into this sort of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a ground of objection, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, because I recall Judge Harhoff saying that Rule 92 ter witnesses would be permitted to testify solely on the basis that there would be no duplication, and any viva voce type evidence would not deal with matters contained within witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That latter explanation is slightly more satisfactory. Actually, what I was going to raise with Madam Sartorio was going to be that it looks like now she's no more tendering exhibits. She's now leading this witness, and is this information she's leading not contained in the statement? What is the point of a 92 ter procedure if now we're going into this kind of leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it was just to clarify what I believe Judge Lattanzi was asking him about in terms of his investigation. I -- I'm not sure that it's clear to the Court and to the Judges what the extent of this person's job and the extent and nature of his investigative work. It doesn't -- I don't think it came across in his answer with the Judge, and I would like to just have him explain the magnitude of his -- of what he had to do and what -- what they did do. I -- I just think it -- the way it was left, it looks like they just looked for people in Ozren and that was the end of I, and I don't believe that's the case. So I would like the witness to be much more detailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would have been helpful to preface your question by saying: "I would like to clarify the point that Judge Lattanzi raised with you."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, we just don't see the connection if you don't say so. So it looks like you're leading this witness, and this witness is supposed to have testified on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So may I proceed or ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Bear in mind what Mr. Robson said. Don't overlap with viva voce evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I just want you to explain to the Judges, without going into what's repeated in your statement, when you were asked by the Judge if you just looked in one particular area -- you need to explain further, please, how extensive your search was and what it involved, in general; Not particular names or persons, but what it involved in general. If it involved interviews, record searches, whatever it involved, please clarify for the Judges the nature of your investigation -- investigative work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to object, but you will have noticed from the witness statements that the witness does deal with these types of issues within the statement. By phrasing a question in such an open and wide manner, and bearing in mind this is supposed to be a time-saving exercise, the witness is inevitably going to overlap on matters contained in the statement, and it's inviting a matter which could last for a significant period of time, I would submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to clarify the method of investigation, I think that's the question. "Now, please clarify for the Judges the nature of your investigation." That's all she's asking for. Do you think it's going to open -- it's a wide question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. When it went on to say if it involved interviews, record searches, whatever, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: -- it's really, in my submission, an invitation to go in -- into this issue at great length.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I didn't even want to refer to that, because I found that to be leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in your hands. What I'm trying to drive at is that in view of the -- the life that 92 ter is a time-saving exercise, I would submit that the question should be focused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have heard that, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. If Your Honours would mind, I would like to focus, as we are allowed to do in 92 ter, on two paragraphs in the witness's statement, if I may, so that the Judges have a clear understanding, while we proceed, what it is I'm asking the witness to -- to -- to clarify. It's the June 2007 statement. It's P -- it's been marked for identification. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In particular, I would like paragraphs 4 and 5. That is on page 2 of each statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you to read paragraphs 4 and 5 briefly, if you may, to yourself.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes, I've done it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And just to --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I want to make -- I want you to make it clear to the Judges what -- exactly what was involved in trying to locate the missing persons.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Can you go back to the fourth paragraph, please. Yes. I believe that this paragraph speaks for itself and says what the role was of the officials of the office and all the persons involved in the search for the missing persons. When the families are provided with information about a lot of their loved ones, whether they're alive or dead, we had to provide them with full information. If we found out that they were in prison, that they had been in prison, we got in touch with the authorities and we agreed on the methodology of the exchange of these persons, and that job was completed in 1996. As of 1996 onwards until this very day, all the persons that have been found were found dead, save for the 15 persons who were on the list who were found on Ozren alive. In order to get hold of the information about the locality of a certain grave, we had to invest a lot of effort and use all the allowed and permissible methods in order to find out where a certain grave was. When the grave was located or when some surface remains were located, at that moment we addressed the competent prosecutor's office, and we requested from the prosecutor to issue an order for the exhumation of those mortal remains. Once such order was received from the prosecutor's office, we would inform the International Commission for Missing Persons as well as the Federal Commission for Missing Persons, and the two of them launched their mechanisms in order to further inform the police. The police come to the spot and secure the location of the -- up to the moment of the exhumation. As far as I know, it is the obligation of the international commission to inform about all the locations, and this is also provided for in various agreements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And can you just -- and, again, I don't want to get into much more detail, sir. But you've been doing this work since 1996; is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I've worked there since 1996; although, I was a member of the Military Commission for Missing Persons from 1993 to 1996. But as of 1996, I've been working with this other commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And are you still continuing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on. Carry on, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was waiting for the Judge to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you still continuing your investigation regarding missing persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to be shown again P02575. Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The same document that he has seen earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to go through another body, Your Honour, unless I admit them -- admit all of the documents in whole, and then we can argue in our closing brief, Your Honour. There's names on this list that we allege match DNA reports, and so I can go through each one individually or we could just admit all of the documents and deal with it in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, all I was asking was are you going back to the same document that we have seen before?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going back to all of the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- unless -- I see Judge Harhoff is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you to refer to number 33 on this list, if you may, and, sir, are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Drago Stjepanovic, he is a missing person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now may the witness be shown P02964 and page 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is a DNA report concerning Drago Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us the name of the wife on this report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Jela Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now may the witness please be shown P02883, page 65 in English and page 33 in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, can you -- can you identify for us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This is a chart for a missing person. In this case, for Stjepanovic Drago, from our database.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you look down - and in the English version, it's there - can you identify what it says as the -- as the wife's name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Jela Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did your -- did your office or did you make a determination about this person with regard to the -- your index card, your -- the DNA, and the list of names? Do you have a conclusion on that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: There is a -- the family took over the body and signed the identification record.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. My specific question, sir, is: What is the connection? Is the person in the DNA report and the person on your index card and the person on the list, are they the -- did you conclude they are the same person or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you just mentioned that the -- the body was turned over to whom?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: It was handed over to the family, who buried the body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now may the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you intend to go through all the names on the list, all 51 of them? I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. It's -- tomorrow, Dr. Brkic will be testifying, who conducted the examination and identification, and there are six bodies that we seek to draw these inferences -- or these conclusions, not inferences. So that's what I was going to go over today. But I -- the -- I will admit the -- the documents in whole. I will ask, seek that they be admitted in whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think you should request this. You were given one hour, and I think you've already spent an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So this has to come to a conclusion; otherwise, we're completely defeating the purpose of having Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir. But these -- these were not specifically referred to in the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why call this witness here, Madam, and tender documents through him if those documents are not referred to in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Because they're additions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If they're additions, get an additional statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've given us a number of statements by this witness, some of which we're going redact. What is the purpose of a 92 ter procedure?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, this is a -- an extremely important witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't dispute that, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I believe that in the statement he identifies the -- the persons that I am talking about today, but we are admitting documents to corroborate and support the witness's statement and testimony. That's what we're seeking to do. At this point I will ask that the -- the three exhibits be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But let me find out from you: When you say "these are additions," are these additions -- do your opposite members have these additions?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We've submitted to them, first of all, disclosure a long, long time ago, as well as an exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are those additions on the e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And have you given them to the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: They're in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why do you need to lead the witness through each one of them?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Because the Defence is disputing that these -- these particular bodies and aspects of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you have used this witness to give his testimony about these bodies in the statement. That's the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, in the statement, there's not a one-on-one connection between the DNA records, the index cards, and the list, which is what I am trying to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if there is no one-on-one connection, what is the purpose of that statement, of what use is it going to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, he concludes in his statement the -- the DNA results, but I'm asking that the documents be admitted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Answer my question, Madam Sartorio. My question is: If his statement does not give a connection between the DNA records, the index cards, and the other lists, of what use is it going to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, because it has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's supposed to be the sum total of his testimony on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, the -- the sum total of what he gave -- we're asking that his statement be admitted because it discusses many things in general, and also it's not disputed what he discusses. But these particular documents were -- were not -- are not connected one-on-one in the statement, and we're allowed in 92 ter to ask questions about additional documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true, ma'am, but the 92 ter is to clarify little things, not to -- you've gone well over your time to present this witness's testimony. The idea was you're just going to ask a few questions and turn him over for cross-examination. I don't see the purpose of the 92 ter procedure if it does not save us the time that you were claiming you're going to save for us. You might as well have led this witness right through.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it -- perhaps that's true, Your Honour, and I'm having the same doubts myself. I wish that I had led the witness through. I think it would have been quite faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And perhaps even clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know whether I understood this witness's testimony today. That's my biggest problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I think if -- I would hope, Your Honours, and -- that between reading the statement and the testimony that -- that it will become clear. But I -- as I said, because I didn't lead the witness through a direct examination to set the background, that he was involved in exhumations and did this and did that, I've had to jump right into the documents that we wanted admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Because the assumption is that background is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's right, and it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. You speak the same language. Maybe you've forgotten that what you are saying is being interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Be that as it may, Your Honour, we have asked that the statements be admitted, and I would like to ask that three pre-trial exhibits be marked as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ma'am, before you ask for pre-trial exhibits to be marked as exhibit, I would like you to give guidance to the Chamber on how to deal with these documents that you have referred to: P02964, page 27, 29, then something about page 17, then there was an official note, page 18, 2575, 2883, 2575 again, 2964 again. Just tell us how to deal with these for purposes of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: For the purposes of the exhibit, we ask that the entire exhibit of -- of 2575 be admitted in evidence. It is two pages long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. And then what about 29 -- in chronology, how they came into evidence: 2964 came before 2575. Can you tell us what to do with 2964.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, we ask that the entire document be admitted in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
