utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to the entire document being admitted into evidence. It's some -- the PT2964 consists of, by my calculations, 13 different documents. Today, we have dipped into three of those documents. I believe one as an order from the prosecutor, the second was another document, and then we've touched upon two DNA reports, two pages of DNA reports. It's a substantial document together; and, in line with the Trial Chamber's previous decisions, I would suggest that we only admit those portions that have been dealt with in evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't that the document that you did admit a little earlier that it did have attachments to it, and you didn't object to it going in with the attachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, you've got an objection, Madam Sartorio. Would you like to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I would, Your Honour. I can -- I can designate certain pages of the -- which includes all of the DNA reports, although each one has not been precisely covered with the witness, but I think there's enough foundation laid. He understands what is these reports are, and I will limit it to that. Dr. Brkic -- I believe this is on the exhibit list for the doctor, and we'll get in the whole exhibit. We referred to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which pages are you going to designate, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Of 2964, we would like the document that starts at page 27 in English and page 14 in Bosnian; and the second document, which is page 29 in English and page 15 in Bosnian. Those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Then pages 17 through 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may mention, madam, today you also attached -- okay. Page 18 is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- included.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: 17 through 25, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There it is, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me, Your Honour, for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so I can clarify, because I don't have page numbers in my document like the Prosecutor does. Page 27 in the English, the -- and page 29, is that the Karahasanovic list?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, that's P02575.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that doesn't mean anything to me. What document would that be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You mean -- the Karahasanovic list is 2575.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. And the first document that was mentioned was --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Those are the orders: The handover, the mortal remains, and the order of the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. And pages 17 to 25 are the DNA reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, we'll go along with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you very much. May P02964 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Honourable Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. May Document P02964 at pages 27 - I'm talking about only the English here - 29, and 17 through to 25 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 645.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Madam Sartorio, the next document that you refer to was P02575.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. We ask that that be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. May P02575 be admitted into evidence and given an Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 646.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the Prosecution requests that P02883 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P02883 is admitted -- Sorry, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm trying to deal with four different PTs at the same time. I've lost track of what that is, so I'd be grateful if my learned friend could explain what that document is before it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: These documents are index cards of the missing persons and index cards of the government of Republika Srpska Office for the Search of Missing and Captured Persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No objection there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did he say objection? Oh, no objection. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry. May we have a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document 2838 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 647.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- I note the time. I just have one more photograph, if I could show the witness, and I'll be finished with the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You show him the photograph, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. P06174.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us where you recognise this photograph from. Do you -- have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I received it in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us from whom you received this photograph.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I got it from the military intelligence services of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'd like you to tell us, if you can, what this document is, what this photograph is of.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This photo was taken on the 17th of September, 1995 and depicts five people whom the families recognised. Of the five person, two are on the aforementioned list. They are Marko Maric. He is the second on the right. The last person is Dragan Lukic, and he's also on the aforementioned list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Just quickly to clarify. When you say "the aforementioned -- sorry, "aforementioned list," which list is that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: I don't know what your number is. The list of -- containing 51 names from Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The handwritten list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, just for the record, for clarification, because it's -- it's -- can you tell us again, starting from the right hand of the document, looking at the photograph, the persons that you identified and which number of what person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give him a pen and ask him to circle them and give them a number. Mr. Robson, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- I think it's the -- the way the question is being formulated. It was put to the witness that "you identified." I don't think the witness has stated that he identified any witness -- any people in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour. I'll withdraw the question. I have a hard copy. Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO and ask the witness to identify the persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, could you just write and put an arrow for the persons that you said - if that's your testimony - that family members had identified.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: The family members have recognised all the five persons. Of the five, two are on the handwritten list. The first one is here, Dragan Lukic; and this person here, that is Marko Maric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you write the name on the list so this document can be admitted into evidence, sir. Write the name of the person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: [Marks] It's not very easy to write like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, do you -- do you know where this document -- photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's plainly a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How is it leading?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I don't know how -- I don't know how it's leading, Your Honour. I'm just asking him if he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How is it leading, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's leading because it's suggesting that he does know where it is. The question could be phrased more neutrally: What do we see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But he has told us what we see. He's told us it's a photograph of five people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: He's told us that members of families identified, told him who these people were as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But how is the question "Do you know where this photograph was taken," leading? How is it leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's inviting an answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you phrase it in such a way that's not inviting an answer, the same question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I would like to, Your Honour, but it's the Prosecution's go at the moment, so I will decline, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, thank you. But if you decline, then I'm going to rule you out of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: Yes. I know where it was taken. It was taken in the former base or the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not the question. The question is: Do you know where it was taken? "Yes, I know," that suffices.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, if you know, where it was taken and how -- and what it is that leads you to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR
utterances.text: This photo was taken in Gostovici in the Mujahedin camp in the house owned by Nestor Ristic. And how do I know that? Behind Marko Maric, if you look, the damage on the wall, in 1997, in November of that year, I had been in that room and I had carried out a reconstruction of that photo, and there was an identical damage on the wall that year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Another trial is coming in here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. We seek to have this document admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 648.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would only like to know: This photograph has been taken on the 17th September 1995; is that so? Perhaps you've said so, but I didn't note it. I don't remember, anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... In the right bottom part is the date which was generated by the camera. You can see the date, the 17th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: After what I'm going to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm going to ask that we all wait until the translation has been made for Judge Lattanzi. The court is going to adjourn now until tomorrow, the 26th, in the same courtroom at 9.00. May we rise.
